misconceptions.description: Treating event 2 (Inform Learners of the Objective) as redundant because the syllabus 'already says it'
misconceptions.trigger: learner argues that explicit objectives at lesson start are unnecessary
misconceptions.feedback: Stating the objective at the lesson level lets the learner mobilize the right strategies and self-monitor. Buried syllabus text does not perform this function.

misconceptions.description: Treating event 3 (Stimulate Recall) as a fun warm-up disconnected from the new content
misconceptions.trigger: learner inserts unrelated trivia at the start of a lesson
misconceptions.feedback: Recall must target the schemas the new content will attach to. If the prior knowledge is not relevant, the event has no information-processing payoff.

misconceptions.description: Believing paraphrasing or clicking 'I understand' satisfies event 6 (Elicit Performance)
misconceptions.trigger: learner equates metacognitive talk with the objective's behavior
misconceptions.feedback: Performance means attempting the actual verb the objective specifies. If the objective is 'compute,' the learner must compute; if 'critique,' the learner must critique.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a high in-session assessment score implies durable retention and transfer
misconceptions.trigger: learner declares a lesson successful based on immediate post-test only
misconceptions.feedback: Without event 9 (Enhance Retention and Transfer) — spaced retrieval, varied practice, explicit transfer prompts — schemas decay within days. In-session scores are necessary but not sufficient.
